evals.name: greenfield-request-response
evals.prompt: i want a telegram bot that takes a city name and replies with the current weather. should remember the last thing each user asked for. set it up so i can deploy it to my cluster the same way as my other stuff
evals.expected_output: A Go bot on telebot v4 storing state in SQLite (not Postgres), with a non-blocking handler, a shared outbound rate limiter, HTML escaping, an ALLOWED_USERS allow list, and a single-replica Recreate deployment.
assertions: Uses telebot v4 (gopkg.in/telebot.v4)
Persists state in SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite, not Postgres or any other server database
Opens SQLite with WAL journal mode and a busy_timeout pragma
The message handler does not block on the weather lookup: it sends a placeholder message and hands the work to a queue or worker, then returns
A single shared outbound rate limiter (golang.org/x/time/rate) paces every send, edit and delete, rather than each call site sending freely
Values interpolated into HTML-mode messages are run through an escape helper
Access is gated by an ALLOWED_USERS allow list, with an empty list explicitly meaning the bot is public
The deployment runs exactly one replica with strategy: Recreate

evals.name: poller-notifier-shape
evals.prompt: need a bot that checks an RSS feed every 15 min and posts new entries to my telegram. just me, one chat. if the feed url starts 404ing i want to be told about it rather than the thing dying quietly
evals.expected_output: A ticker-driven watcher on telebot v4, pinned to one CHAT_ID, deduping in SQLite, escaping untrusted feed text, pacing bulk posts through a shared limiter, deployed as one Recreate replica.
assertions: Uses telebot v4 (gopkg.in/telebot.v4)
Posts to a single chat ID pinned in configuration, and ignores updates arriving from any other chat
Persists which entries were already sent in SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite, so a restart does not re-post old entries
Opens SQLite with WAL journal mode and a busy_timeout pragma
Feed-supplied text (titles, descriptions) is escaped before being interpolated into an HTML-mode message
Posting a batch of new entries is paced by a shared outbound rate limiter rather than sent in an unthrottled loop
The deployment runs exactly one replica with strategy: Recreate

evals.name: extend-existing-bot
evals.prompt: my go telegram bot currently just replies to /start. i want to add a /stats command that shows how many requests each user has made this week, and it needs to survive restarts. where does that code go?
evals.expected_output: Counts persisted in SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite on a real volume, the /stats handler not blocking the update loop on the query, and usernames escaped before rendering.
assertions: Recommends SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite for the counts rather than Postgres or an in-memory store
The /stats handler does not block the update loop on an unbounded query: the call is bounded by a timeout or handed off
Usernames or other user-supplied text are escaped before being interpolated into the rendered stats message
States that surviving restarts requires the database file to sit on a real volume, not the container filesystem
Notes that the deployment must stay at one replica with strategy: Recreate rather than scaling out
